name: South Africa
headline: The potential of a continent, the fractures of its history.
summary: South Africa is the world's most unequal large economy. Apartheid left a spatial and educational structure that still weighs on productivity. Yet the country holds strategic minerals, solid financial institutions, and a vigorous civil society.

history.title: Union of South Africa
history.text: The British and Boer colonies unite. Political power is reserved for whites, while gold and diamond mines finance industrialization.

history.title: Institutionalization of apartheid
history.text: The National Party systematizes racial segregation. The Black majority loses political rights, land, and quality education.

history.title: The Sharpeville massacre
history.text: Police open fire on protesters against pass laws. The massacre internationalizes the anti-apartheid cause and radicalizes the struggle.

history.title: First democratic elections
history.text: Nelson Mandela becomes president. The negotiated transition averts civil war but does not radically redistribute wealth.

history.title: The 1996 Constitution
history.text: One of the world's most protective constitutions guarantees rights, an independent judiciary, and watchdog institutions.

history.title: The football World Cup
history.text: The country demonstrates its logistics capacity and soft power. Infrastructure improves, but inequality and unemployment remain massive.

history.title: Government of national unity
history.text: The ANC loses its majority. A coalition with the opposition opens a period of political instability, but also hope for reforms.

institutions.executive: President elected by Parliament; coalition government since 2024
institutions.legislature: Bicameral Parliament: National Assembly and National Council of Provinces
institutions.central_bank: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), independent and inflation-targeting
institutions.law: A hybrid of common law, Roman-Dutch law, and constitutional law
institutions.fact: The 1996 Constitution is often cited as one of the most protective of social rights in the world.

allies.name: Brazil / India / China
allies.note: Cooperation within BRICS and major emerging economies.

allies.name: African Union
allies.note: A driving role in continental diplomacy.

allies.name: European Union
allies.note: Leading trade partner and source of investment.

rivals.name: Nigeria
rivals.note: Competition for African leadership and investment.

rivals.name: United States
rivals.note: Recent diplomatic tensions over foreign and trade policies.

dependencies.name: China
dependencies.note: Top buyer of minerals and largest supplier of goods.

dependencies.name: Electricity
dependencies.note: The Eskom crisis and blackouts weigh on activity.

gdp_growth.note: Growth is near zero: power cuts, rail logistics, and weak confidence weigh on investment.

inflation.note: Inflation is back within the SARB target (3-6%), which allowed rates to start coming down.

debt_gdp.note: Debt is rising on deficits and the Eskom bailout. Interest costs absorb a growing share of the budget.

policy_rate.note: The policy rate stays high to anchor expectations. Credit is expensive for households and small firms.

unemployment.note: Unemployment tops 30%, with extreme depth among the young. It is the main social and political risk.

reserves.note: Reserves cover about five months of imports. They support the rand but cannot absorb a lasting shock.

rating.note: The rating sits in speculative territory. Strong institutions and moderate debt limit the premium, but weak growth weighs.

cds.note: The market prices more risk than Morocco's, reflecting weak growth, unemployment, and fiscal strains.

equity_index.note: The index benefits from gold, mining, and financials. The stock market outperforms the real economy.

currency.name: Rand
currency.note: The rand is liquid but volatile. It serves as a proxy for emerging-market risk and stays sensitive to commodity prices.

strengths: Wealth in strategic minerals and renewable energy.
One of Africa's freest civil societies and presses.
risks: Mass unemployment and inequalities inherited from apartheid.
An energy and logistics crisis that rations output.
A fragile governing coalition and fiscal risk.
opportunities: Minerals for the energy transition (platinum, manganese, vanadium).
A financial and logistics hub for Southern Africa.

quiz.question: Which event marked the end of political apartheid in South Africa?
quiz.explanation: The first multiracial elections of 1994 bring Nelson Mandela to power. Apartheid is abolished, but its economic and spatial legacy persists.
